entry.value: Input table containing data to be processed

Metanode creates correlation coefficients heatmap, optionally with hieararchical clustering on selected columns. The central part consists of correlation coefficients for each column pair displayed as heatmap. Plus coefficients are clustered using hierarchical clustering where columns with highest correlation should cluster together. %%00010%%00010You can select correlation coefficient type to be computed. Correlation coefficients can be displayed using different colormaps to highlight the differences. Colormap center (e.g. what number should be visualized as centered color in the concrete colormap) can be manually selected, otherwise it will be computed automaticaly and colormap will start at minmum and end at maximum number. Used colormap names can be checked here: https://matplotlib.org/users/colormaps.html. %%00010%%00010Cluster analysis has these two settings: %%00010- distance metric - how the distance between the two columns should be calculated, e.g. euclidian, cityblock...%%00010%%00010- cluster method - method for calculating the distances between clusters, e.g. complete, average...%%00010%%00010In a clustered heatmap, it is possible to split the columns into a selected number of groups based on the created dendrograms. Groups will be visually denoted in the clustermap and also described in the bottom table output.%%00010%%00010Note: any data preprocessing (like transformation, normalization) should be done prior the metanode usage! %%00010%%00010================= %%00010%%00010Used programs and tools and their respective licenses at the time of the metanode creation.
